entry.title: Taskbar Calendar Week Numbers 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Calendar Week Numbers

Adds a week number column to the calendar flyout that opens when you click the clock in the Windows 11 taskbar, like the week numbers in Outlook.

Settings

  • Week numbering: ISO 8601 (default; used in Germany and most of Europe) or the first-week-of-year rule from the Windows regional settings.
  • Column header: text above the column. Empty means automatic ("KW" for a German Windows display language, "Wk" otherwise). A single space hides it.
  • Week number color: the Windows accent color (default, the same color as today's date) or the normal text color.
  • Column width, font size and opacity of the week numbers.

Notes

  • Only the calendar flyout is changed. The mod writes nothing to disk and makes no network requests.
  • The calendar's day cells get slightly narrower to make room for the column.
  • The calendar flyout is hosted in ShellExperienceHost.exe. Tested on Windows 11 build 26220.

entry.title: DynamicDock 1.0
entry.content:
DynamicDock

Best for use with ultrawide monitors, but works on any monitor. Instead of the taskbar popping up in the middle of the screen, the taskbar appears or slides the icons to your mouse right where your mouse touches the screens edge.

This is still the real Windows taskbar, so everything works like normal: jump lists (right-click), hover thumbnails, badges, drag and drop, the tray and the clock.

Bottom taskbars (works with auto-hide or always visible)

  1. Choose how the taskbar shows:
    • Auto-hide: confirm or turn on Automatically hide the taskbar in Windows Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors > Select "Automatically hide the taskbar" from the menu.
    • Always visible: this mod also works with the default bottom taskbar that is always visible. Be sure to turn on Keep the bottom Windows default taskbar full width in the Bottom taskbar settings.
  2. Keep Taskbar alignment on Center.
  3. Move the mouse to the bottom edge of the screen anywhere: the bar opens under it or simply slides the icons to your mouse with the default taskbar.
  • Keep in mind that taskbars change widths based on the amount of icons in the bar. Some additional adjustments may be required as the total taskbar pixel count changes to maintain functionality and spacing as you desire.

Top taskbar

  1. In Windows Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors, set Taskbar position to Top. This option only exists in recent Windows 11 builds (for example 26200.9711). If your build doesn't have it, use the Taskbar on top for Windows 11 mod to move the taskbar to the top.
  2. In DynamicDock's settings, open Top taskbar and turn on Taskbar on top of screen.
  3. Touch the top edge of the screen anywhere: the app icons slide under the mouse.
  • The taskbar itself stays full width across the top (Windows can't auto-hide it there), and the tray and clock stay at the right edge. Only the row of app icons moves, so nothing collapses or leaves empty space.
  • The center zone, limits, edge distance and smooth movement work the same. The icons never slide under the tray.
  • The Tray and clock and Rounded corners settings are for the compact bottom bar only and are ignored for the top taskbar option.

Full-width bottom taskbar

Prefer the taskbar to stay full width at the bottom too? Turn on Keep the bottom taskbar full width (in the Bottom taskbar section). The taskbar then works like the top one: it pops up full width with Widgets in the left corner and the tray and clock at the right edge, and only the app icons slide to the mouse.

Compatibility

  • Works with the default Windows 11 taskbar and with the Windows 11 Taskbar Styler mod (DynamicDock moves the bar; the styler keeps deciding how it looks).
  • Settings marked (default taskbar only) change the look of the plain Windows taskbar. When Taskbar Styler or a similar mod restyles the taskbar, those settings are skipped so they don't fight that mod's look.
  • Other taskbar mods (icon size, clock customization, auto-hide instant show, thumbnail reorder) can be used alongside it. Taskbar auto-hide instant show is recommended: it removes Windows' delay before the taskbar pops up.
  • Windows 11 only.

Troubleshooting (Try this if things are not working correctly)

  • The bar doesn't move, or the taskbar looks stuck in a moved position: turn DynamicDock off and on again in Windhawk. If that doesn't fix it, restart Explorer: open Task Manager, search for Windows Explorer, right-click Windows Explorer and choose Restart. This rebuilds the taskbar from scratch (it also closes open File Explorer windows). You may need to tap your windows key on the keyboard for the taskbar to reappear. Then return to windhawk and toggle your mods on/off as needed to function properly.
  • After installing or updating the mod, the first touch of the screen edge can take a moment while DynamicDock finds the taskbar.
  • To report a problem, turn on Debug logging on the mod's Advanced tab, reproduce it, and share the lines from the mod's log. You should see logs being created as you tap the screen edge in different places.

entry.title: Lock Screen Clock Styler 0.4.0
entry.content:
Lock Screen Clock Styler

Customize and enhance the Windows 11 lock screen clock with modern designs, frosted glass panels, dynamic date capsules, and clean layout controls.

Features:

  • Minimalist Sonoma (Clean Typography): Apple-inspired lock screen typography with date positioned above the time, slender display numerals, dual-layer atmospheric shadow, and bottom-left or center placement.
  • Modern Flip Clock: Split glass cards for hour and minute with an elegant horizontal flip seam.
  • Classic Flip Clock: Classic mechanical Solari-inspired flip clock with matte charcoal flap cards, aged ivory cream typography, mechanical split seam, and hinge axle clips.
  • Cyberpunk Sci-Fi HUD Terminal: Bespoke tactical Netrunner HUD terminal with dark obsidian glass chassis, tactical corner brackets in acid yellow and hot magenta, top telemetry diagnostic bar, electric cyan digits with rhythmic tactical pulse, and bottom telemetry date logger.
  • Retro Pixel / LED Dot Matrix Clock: Authentic dot matrix display inspired by classic digital boards with active and ambient inactive LED dots.
  • Minimalist Aura / Floating Clock: Frameless floating typography with ambient soft drop-shadow depth and an elegant frosted date pill.
  • Battery & Charging Capsule: Live battery percentage and power indicator (⚡ %85) for laptop users, automatically hidden on desktop PCs.
  • 12-Hour / 24-Hour Format: Switch between 24-hour time and 12-hour time with dedicated AM/PM indicators across themes.
  • Show Seconds Toggle: Optional live seconds display. Supported by every style except the two flip clocks.
  • Frosted Glass / Acrylic Styling: Translucent glass panels with subtle border highlights and rounded corners.
  • Dynamic Date Display: Elegant date and day capsule positioned beneath or above the clock, adapting to the user's system locale.
  • Hide Default Widgets: Clean up the lock screen by hiding MSN weather, sports, and news widgets.
  • Hide / Replace Default Clock: Seamlessly replace the stock Windows 11 clock with custom styles or adjust vertical offsets.
  • Extensive Customization: Card opacity, font size, vertical offsets, and alignments are fully customizable via settings.
  • No XAML Diagnostics: The mod walks the lock screen visual tree from its own UI thread instead of registering a XAML Diagnostics TAP. It can therefore run alongside other XAML-based Windhawk mods such as Windows 11 Start Menu Styler.

Screenshots:

| Style | Preview | | :---: | :---: | | Minimalist Sonoma | | | Retro Pixel / LED Matrix | | | Modern Flip Clock | | | Classic Flip Clock | | | Cyberpunk Sci-Fi HUD | |

Security Note:

This mod exclusively targets LockApp.exe. It does not inject into or interfere with LogonUI.exe or winlogon.exe in the Secure Desktop, preventing any system lockup or logon security risks.

entry.title: Enter to Rename in File Explorer 0.4.0
entry.content:
Enter to Rename in File Explorer

Use Enter to rename a selected file or folder in Windows File Explorer, like in macOS Finder. Press Enter again to confirm the new name. The standard F2 shortcut is unchanged.

Scope

  • Works only in File Explorer windows, not on the desktop or in file dialogs, and only when the keyboard focus appears to be inside Explorer's shell file list.
  • Does not intercept Enter while editing text, in the address/search controls, or with Ctrl, Alt, or Shift pressed.
  • This mod intentionally does not remap Ctrl+Enter to open a file.

Compatibility

Tested by the original user on Windows 11 for files, folders, rename confirmation, search, and multi-selection. Other Windows versions, Explorer extensions and alternative list controls have not yet been validated.

Notes

The mod intercepts Enter and synthesizes an F2 key press. The context check is based on Explorer window classes, which might differ across builds. If the mod causes unintended behavior, disable it in Windhawk.

entry.title: Refined Quick Settings and Sound 0.1.154
entry.content:
Refined Quick Settings and Sound

This "vanilla+" Windhawk mod reworks the Windows 11 "Quick Settings" and "Volume mixer" panels and makes them fit for daily use. It follows the Windows 11 design language, refining existing features and adding new ones: thin sliders, even row spacing at every display scale and a smooth frame transition to the Sound page.

Everything runs inside the shell's own panels (ShellHost): no extra windows, the system Acrylic, fonts, themes, lists, bindings and animations are kept, and customizations are restored when the mod is unloaded.

Features

Quick Settings

  • Brightness control for DDC/CI-compatible displays, with animated glyphs.
  • Press the brightness glyph to toggle night light on and off.
  • Open display settings directly from the glyph on the right side of the slider.

Sound

  • The "Sound output" page is now simply "Sound".
  • Change the output and input devices and the spatial sound provider from dropdown lists.
  • Below them, a reworked Volume mixer for the apps. It is collapsible and remembers its last state.
  • Mouse wheel on every slider; press an app's icon to mute and restore it, or its volume number to set it to 100.
  • Hide apps from the mixer by name (setting below).

Taskbar

  • Click the volume icon to open Sound directly.
  • The system's animated volume glyph and an Ethernet glyph for wired networks.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11 24H2 or later (Quick Settings hosted by ShellHost), x86-64 (ARM64 is untested). Development testing: build 26300, primarily at 125% scale.
  • Other Windows builds and display scales need validation. The mod depends on internal shell XAML elements and symbols which can change with Windows updates.
  • DDC/CI brightness requires a compatible monitor with DDC/CI enabled.
  • Added labels such as "Sound" and "Input device" are in English.
  • The first Sound opening in each ShellHost process starts with the mixer collapsed; subsequent openings remember its state.

Control Center discovery uses COM-interface symbol hooks in ControlCenter.dll and the public XAML visual tree; it does not open a XAML Diagnostics connection. Compatibility with other mods that edit the same controls still requires live testing. If the panel was already open when enabling the mod, close and reopen it; restart ShellHost if it is not picked up.

Notes

Disable other mods that change the Quick Settings, the Sound page or the taskbar volume icon before enabling this one. Errors are written to the Windhawk log.

Credits and license

GPL-3.0-only. The UI-thread dispatch technique follows m417z's Notification Center Styler (GPL-3.0). ControlCenter.dll discovery uses the COM produce-interface pattern documented by Per-monitor brightness. The hidden-applications parser is adapted from the local Sound Output Direct and Taller mod (GPL-3.0-only). The sliders-horizontal and ethernet-port icons are from Lucide (ISC); the license notice is included below in this source file.

entry.title: Mute Focused Window 1.0
entry.content:
Mute Focused Window

Press Ctrl+Alt+M to mute the app whose window has focus. Press it again to unmute it. Other apps keep playing.

This changes the same per-app mute as the Windows Volume Mixer, so the mixer shows the result and can undo it.

What gets muted

The mod mutes every audio session that belongs to the focused window's app, on every active output device. If some of those sessions are muted and others are not, the first press mutes them all.

Browsers and Electron apps such as Discord play sound from a helper process instead of the process that owns the window. The mod therefore includes the app's background child processes too. A child process with its own visible window is treated as a separate app and left alone. For example, a media player launched from a terminal keeps playing when you mute the terminal.

Hotkey

Change the hotkey in the mod's settings. Write any modifiers and exactly one key, joined by +, for example Ctrl+Alt+M, Win+Shift+F9 or Pause.

  • Modifiers: Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win.
  • Keys: A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24, Space, Tab, Enter, Esc, Backspace, Insert, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Up, Down, Left, Right, Pause, ScrollLock, PrintScreen, Numpad0– Numpad9, VolumeMute, VolumeDown, VolumeUp, MediaPlayPause, MediaNext, MediaPrev, MediaStop.
  • Any other key: its virtual-key code in hexadecimal, such as 0x4D.

Windows gives a hotkey to only one program at a time, and other apps stop receiving that key combination. If the hotkey does nothing, another program may already own it. Turn on logging in the mod's Advanced tab to see why.

The default, Ctrl+Alt+M, also takes Word's Insert Comment shortcut. On keyboard layouts with an AltGr key, Windows treats AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so AltGr+M (µ on German layouts) stops typing its character. Choose another hotkey if you need either.

Using the keyboard's Mute key

Most keyboards with a dedicated Mute key, and laptops with a mute function key, send VolumeMute.

  • Set the hotkey to VolumeMute to make the Mute key mute the focused app instead of everything. Also turn on Mute the system when there's no app to mute, so the key still mutes everything when you press it on the desktop, the taskbar, a File Explorer window or an app without audio.
  • Set the hotkey to Ctrl+VolumeMute to keep the Mute key as it is and use Ctrl+Mute for the focused app.

Keyboard software that reassigns the Mute key can stop it from sending VolumeMute.

Limitations

  • A browser is muted as a whole, not tab by tab. The Volume Mixer shows it the same way.
  • An app started from the focused app and hidden in the tray, with no visible window, counts as part of the focused app. For example, a music player started from a launcher and minimized to the tray is muted along with the launcher. Windows gives no reliable way to tell such an app from the hidden helper processes that browsers and Electron apps play their sound through.
  • Windows remembers an app's mute setting. An app you muted is still muted the next time it starts; press the hotkey or use the Volume Mixer to unmute it.
  • Pressing the hotkey on the desktop, the taskbar or a File Explorer window does nothing, unless Mute the system when there's no app to mute is on.
  • That system mute doesn't show Windows' volume indicator.

entry.title: Bulk Copy File and Folder Names 0.3.0
entry.content:
Bulk Copy File and Folder Names

Windows has Copy as path (Ctrl+Shift+C), but it gives you full paths in quotes, and often you only want the names. This mod copies the names of the files and folders you select in File Explorer as plain text, one per line. It works on one item or on many at once. A selection can mix files and folders.

Right-click menu

Right-click a file, a folder, or a selection of many files and folders in a File Explorer window. The classic menu gets two entries, Copy name and Copy name without extension. On Windows 11 they're in the menu you get from Show more options or Shift+right-click. The entries are on by default, and you can turn them off in the settings.

Copy name without extension keeps folder names whole, so sub.folder stays sub.folder, and a.tar.gz becomes a.tar. A name that starts with a dot, like .gitignore, stays whole.

Hotkeys

The hotkeys are off until you turn them on, so a fresh install takes no key away from File Explorer. To turn them on, open the mod's Settings tab in Windhawk, tick Hotkeys, and save. The defaults are Ctrl+Shift+Y for names with extensions and Ctrl+Shift+U for names without. You can change both keys there too.

A key is handled inside the File Explorer window that has the focus, so it never reaches other programs. It does nothing while you type in a rename box, the address bar or the search box, and it does nothing when no file or folder is selected. In both cases the key goes to File Explorer as usual.

If you pick a key that File Explorer already uses, like Ctrl+Shift+N for New folder, the mod wins while the hotkeys are on and something is selected.

Settings

  • Hotkeys: turn the two key combinations on. Off by default.
  • Modifiers and key for each copy action. Ctrl+Alt and Ctrl+Alt+Shift also match AltGr, so skip them if your keyboard layout types letters with AltGr.
  • Separator: a new line, a comma, or a space between names.
  • Quote names: put each name in double quotes.
  • Right-click menu: show the two menu entries. On by default.

Limits

  • The keys and menu entries don't work on the desktop or in file dialogs. Only File Explorer windows count.
  • The Windows 11 compact menu can't take new entries from a mod. Use Show more options.
  • The menu entries don't show on the column header menu, the menu you get from empty space in a folder, or the menu you get after a drag with the right mouse button.
  • Items that aren't files or folders, like drives in This PC, give their internal name.
  • If nothing is selected, nothing happens.

Tutorial

  1. Select the files and folders in a File Explorer window. A mix of both is fine.
  2. Hold Shift and right-click the selection. Pick Copy name or Copy name without extension.
  3. Paste. Copy name gives you every name with its extension, one per line.
  4. Copy name without extension drops the extension from files and keeps the full name of folders.
  5. If you'd rather use the keyboard, tick Hotkeys in the settings. Ctrl+Shift+Y then does what Copy name does, and Ctrl+Shift+U does what Copy name without extension does.

Gotchas

  • In step 2, the compact Windows 11 menu can't show the entries. Use Shift+right-click or Show more options.
  • In step 4, only the last extension goes, so archive.tar.gz becomes archive.tar.
  • In step 5, a key does nothing while you type in a rename box, the address bar or the search box, and nothing while no item is selected. File Explorer gets the key instead.

Credits

The way the hotkeys are caught, a hook on TranslateAcceleratorW that steps aside while a text box has the focus, follows the approach of the Explorer Custom Shortcuts mod.

entry.title: Fullscreen Start (Launchpad style) 1.0.0
entry.content:
Fullscreen Start (Launchpad style)

Replaces the Windows Start menu with a screen in the style of the macOS Launchpad: all installed apps in a grid, with search at the top and a blurred background.

Features

  • Fullscreen: takes the whole work area of the monitor where the mouse is, without covering the taskbar, other side bars or the Dock of the Standalone Dock (macOS-like) mod.
  • All apps: the same ones as the "All apps" list of Start (programs and Store apps), in alphabetical order, with icon and name.
  • Search: just type. The list is filtered instantly, ignoring case and accents; names that start with the text come first.
  • Adjustable blurred background: configurable strength, opacity and color.

How to open

Everything that would open the Windows Start menu opens this one instead:

  • the Windows key and Ctrl+Esc;
  • the Start button of the taskbar, or of the Dock of the Standalone Dock mod.

The mod hooks the function Explorer uses to show Start (XamlLauncher::ShowStartView in twinui.pcshell.dll), so the original Start doesn't open at all. Windhawk downloads the symbols of that file the first time the mod loads.

Keyboard and mouse

  • Type to search; Backspace deletes, Ctrl+Backspace deletes the last word, Ctrl+V pastes.
  • Arrows select an app, Enter opens the selected one (while searching, the first result is already selected).
  • Esc clears the search; with an empty search, it closes.
  • The mouse wheel or Page Up/Page Down scroll the list.
  • Clicking outside the icons or switching windows closes it.

Blur

  • Adjustable (default): the mod takes a screenshot the moment it opens and blurs it with the chosen strength. The background stays still while Start is open.
  • Acrylic and Windows blur: the effect is applied by DWM composition and follows what changes behind it. Windows doesn't allow changing the strength of that blur, so the strength setting doesn't apply to them.
  • No blur: only the color on top.

Changes to the settings apply the next time Start opens.

entry.title: Middle-click empty tab bar to open a new tab (Chrome/Edge/Brave) 1.0
entry.content:
Middle-click empty tab bar to open a new tab (Chrome/Edge/Brave)

Middle-click the empty area of the tab bar (between the "+" button and the minimize/maximize/close buttons) to open a new tab, just like clicking "+".

Currently supported browsers: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave. Other Chromium-based browsers may work too: add their executable in the mod's Advanced settings (custom process inclusion list).

The empty tab bar area is detected using the window's hit-testing: Chrome reports it as a caption (draggable) area, while tabs and buttons are reported as client area. By default, only caption areas that have a tab or a button between them and the side away from the window buttons are used, so the thin drag strip above the tabs and the area before the first tab are ignored. This also works with right-to-left UI languages, where the tab bar is mirrored.

Installed web apps (PWAs) are ignored, since they have a title bar instead of a tab bar.

The new tab is opened with the browser's "new" app command (the same command as Ctrl+T), so no keyboard input is simulated.

entry.title: Middle Click New Tab 1.0.0
entry.content:
The mod opens a new tab when you release the middle mouse button over the empty space of a tab strip.

Three apps are supported:

  • File Explorer: the new tab is opened by invoking the native AddButton (fallback: Ctrl+T).
  • Notepad: the new tab is opened by invoking the native AddButton (fallback: Ctrl+N).
  • Terminal: the new tab is opened by invoking the native AddButton (fallback: Ctrl+Shift+T). Note: This does not work if Terminal is running as administrator due to privilege isolation.

You can enable or disable each app individually in the mod's settings tab.

How it works:

  • The mod runs as a standalone Windhawk Tool, ensuring it executes in a single instance and doesn't inject multiple hooks into different Explorer processes.
  • A dedicated low-level mouse hook thread records middle-button press/release events. It never performs slow UI Automation work and never blocks global input.
  • If the press looks like it happened in a tab strip area, an isolated UI Automation worker thread verifies whether the point is on an actual tab, a button, or empty tab strip space.
  • If the mouse button is released before the check finishes, the mod temporarily holds the release event and re-sends it synthetically after the check. This avoids the race condition where the native app closes the tab before the mod can inspect it.
  • Middle clicking an actual tab or the add button is left untouched, so the native behaviors keep working perfectly.

entry.title: Notification Bell Highlighter 0.5.2
entry.content:
Notification Bell Highlighter

Makes the Windows notification bell more obvious when notifications are waiting. Draws a pulsing, bright overlay with an optional counter over the taskbar notification bell when notifications are pending.

Settings for shape (circle or square), size, position, colour, pulse rate and counter visibility

Windows 11 only. Tested on 26H2 build 26300.9711.

Limitations:

  • Overlay rather than restyled icon, this mod highlights the bell, while 'Taskbar tray system icon tweaks' can hide it.
  • Primary taskbar only.
  • Relies on the English accessible name, e.g. "Notifications 1 new notification".

entry.title: Smart Process Priority & RAM Optimizer 1.0.1
entry.content:
Smart Process Priority & RAM Optimizer

Dynamically manages process priorities and memory allocation to keep foreground applications responsive and prevent background tasks from causing system hitches.

Expectations

  • What it does: Mitigates micro-stutters and input latency spikes caused by background processes competing for CPU resources.
  • What it does not do: It does not increase maximum hardware performance or raw gaming FPS.
  • Plug & Play: Safe, balanced defaults work out of the box without requiring any configuration.
  • Advanced tuning: Deeper options (e.g. EcoQoS, P/E-core affinity, power plans) are disabled by default.

Key Features

1. Foreground Priority Boost

  • Elevates the CPU priority of the active window and its related child processes.
  • Optionally assigns the active application to performance cores on hybrid CPU architectures.

2. Background Throttling

  • Temporarily reduces the CPU priority of background processes exceeding defined utilization thresholds.
  • Optionally restricts throttled tasks to efficiency cores or applies Windows EcoQoS.

3. Audio & Network Protection

  • Shields processes with active audio playback from throttling and memory trimming via WASAPI real-time peak metering.
  • Intelligently distinguishes sustained media playback from transient notification sounds or terminal bells.
  • Shields processes performing active network transfers from throttling.

4. Compute & AI Workload Protection

  • Prevents throttling of intensive background computation, shader compilation, and local AI inference tasks.

5. Memory Optimization

  • Gradually trims unused working set memory from idle applications via Windows memory APIs.
  • Automatically suspends trimming on battery power and during post-sleep transitions.
  • Includes a configurable hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+F11) with audio confirmation for manual memory cleanup.

6. Dynamic Power Scheme

  • Automatically engages the High Performance power plan during demanding workloads on AC power.
  • Note: Switches the system-wide power plan for all users. The original plan is restored upon returning to desktop or when the mod is disabled. If the PC crashes, loses power, or if a user signs out while High Performance is active, the plan can stay active until the mod restarts (or permanently if the mod is removed while engaged).

7. Inactive Browser Tab Trimming

  • Detects dormant background browser renderers and trims their unused memory while keeping active tabs intact.
  • Dynamically adapts to multi-process browser architectures (Chromium, Gecko, etc.) without hardcoded process names.

Settings

All settings are optional and pre-configured for balanced out-of-the-box use. Advanced options (e.g. EcoQoS, P/E-core affinity, power schemes) can be enabled in the mod settings if desired.

  • Foreground priority boost (ProBalance): Automatically increases the CPU priority of the active foreground window.
  • Suggest P-cores to foreground window: Directs the active foreground app to Performance Cores on hybrid CPUs.
  • Dynamic high-performance power scheme: Temporarily activates the High Performance power scheme for demanding workloads on AC power.
  • Throttle CPU-heavy background processes: Temporarily lowers priority of background processes consuming excessive CPU.
  • Restrict throttled background apps to E-cores: Confines throttled background tasks to Efficiency Cores on hybrid CPUs.
  • Windows efficiency mode (EcoQoS): Applies Windows power throttling to background processes.
  • Audio & music protection shield: Protects applications actively streaming or playing audio against throttling and memory sweeps.
  • Network activity shield: Protects applications actively downloading or streaming data.
  • Protect local AI & shader compilers: Prevents throttling during local AI inference (Ollama, LM Studio) and shader compilation.
  • Process startup grace period: Minimum age in seconds a newly spawned process must reach before being eligible for memory trimming or priority throttling (default: 5 seconds).
  • Standard free RAM threshold: Percentage of available physical memory below which background memory cleanup is triggered (0 = Auto-Adaptive).
  • Inactive browser tabs memory trim: Reclaims unused memory from dormant background browser renderer tabs.
  • Early memory cap for heavy apps: Reclaims memory from listed heavy apps once their memory exceeds the configured cap.
  • Emergency clean hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+F11): Triggers an immediate memory reclamation pass with optional audio confirmation.
  • Excluded processes: Comma-separated list of executable names that must never be throttled or trimmed.

Compatibility

  • Supported OS: Windows 11 (all versions including 24H2).
  • Windows 10: Untested and unsupported (not officially validated, though core Win32 APIs may function).
  • Supported Architectures: x86 (32-bit), x64 (64-bit), and ARM64.
  • Compatible with standard and hybrid Intel/AMD CPUs (P/E-cores).
  • Avoid running alongside similar tools (e.g. Process Lasso, Mem Reduct) to prevent conflicting adjustments.

Support

If you find this mod useful, you can support its development and maintenance:

  • Support on Ko-fi

Credits & Acknowledgments

  • Process Lasso (Bitsum): Inspiration for the ProBalance concept and foreground responsiveness prioritization.
  • LiveTuner (LT): Inspiration for dynamic real-time priority tuning heuristics.
  • ISLC (Intelligent Standby List Cleaner by Wagnardsoft): Inspiration for adaptive threshold triggers and gaming memory management.
  • Mem Reduct (Henry++): Inspiration for safe working-set trimming techniques.

entry.title: Multi PrintScreen 1.0.0
entry.content:
Multi PrintScreen

Take several screenshots in a row (Win+Shift+S, PrintScreen, …), then press Ctrl+V repeatedly in a target app: the first screenshot is pasted first, the second on the next Ctrl+V, and so on (First In, First Out).

How it works (short version):

  • A hidden window in a dedicated tool process listens for clipboard changes (AddClipboardFormatListener) and copies pure screenshot payloads (CF_DIB and PNG) into a private FIFO queue.
  • Only pure screenshots are queued. Copying anything else (text, Excel cells, files, HTML) automatically clears the queue so Ctrl+V never interferes with normal copy/paste.
  • A low-level keyboard hook swallows Ctrl+V (in any application) when the queue is not empty, puts the oldest screenshot onto the clipboard, then re-sends a marked V keystroke so the app pastes it.
  • Windows Clipboard History (Win+V) duplicates are suppressed for re-injected pastes.
  • When the queue is empty, Ctrl+V behaves completely normally.

Runs as a dedicated tool process in Windhawk. Nothing is injected into explorer.exe or into the apps you paste into, so there is nothing to marshal across processes.

Memory limits:

  • Total queue memory is capped at 128 MB (the oldest screenshots are dropped if this budget is exceeded). Individual image payloads above 32 MB are skipped.

Note: When pasting, the physical 'V' keystroke is swallowed while the image is restored to the clipboard, then re-injected. Very fast typing immediately after Ctrl+V may occasionally land before the pasted image.

entry.title: Modern Run Dialog UI For Windows 11 2.0.15
entry.content:
Modern Run Dialog UI For Windows 11

Modern Run Dialog UI Preview

🌐 English

Modern Run Dialog UI For Windows 11 replaces the classic Win32 Run (Win + R) dialog with a sleek, borderless Fluent Design / Command Palette interface tailored for Windows 11.

✨ Key Features

  • Fluent UI & Acrylic Blur:

  • Completely removes the classic title bar and legacy window frames while preserving native Windows 11 rounded corners.

  • Full-window Acrylic Blur background with customizable opacity.

  • GDI+ 32-bit ARGB (Premultiplied Alpha) rendering engine with crisp system Segoe UI typography and full Per-Monitor DPI scaling.

  • Smart History List:

  • Displays up to 5 recently executed commands right above the input bar.

  • Automatically extracts native application icons and friendly application names in the command - App Name format.

  • Shows the last executed timestamp next to the history clock icon on each row (stored cleanly in Windhawk mod storage).

  • Supports single-click to fill the input box, double-click to execute immediately, or Up / Down (↑ / ↓) arrow keys to cycle through history.

  • Modern Input Bar & Action Buttons:

  • Borderless single-line input box with automatic horizontal scrolling for long file paths.

  • Browse Button (Browse 📁): Opens the native Windows file picker (*.exe, *.bat, *.cmd, *.msc, *.cpl) and inserts the full path into the input bar.

  • Run (Run ↵) & Exit (Exit ✕) Buttons: High-contrast Fluent accent buttons with smooth hover and press states.

  • Quality-of-Life Fixes:

  • Taskbar Icon Click to Minimize / Restore: Click the Run icon on the Taskbar to minimize (hide) or restore the Run window like a normal app.

  • Win + R Toggle: Pressing Win + R while the Run dialog is open will immediately close it (or restore it if minimized).

  • Flawless IME Input: Works seamlessly with Windows IME (Vietnamese Telex/VNI, CJK) and Unikey without composition glitches.

  • Multilingual Interface:

  • Automatically detects the Windows UI language or lets you manually choose from 10 languages.

🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt

Modern Run Dialog UI For Windows 11 thay thế hộp thoại Run (Win + R) cổ điển bằng giao diện Fluent Design / Command Palette hiện đại, không viền và trong suốt chuẩn Windows 11.

✨ Tính năng nổi bật

  • Giao diện Fluent & Kính mờ (Acrylic Blur):

  • Loại bỏ thanh tiêu đề và khung viền cổ điển, giữ góc bo tròn tự nhiên của Windows 11.

  • Làm mờ nền trong suốt (Acrylic Blur) toàn cửa sổ, tùy chỉnh độ trong suốt linh hoạt.

  • Kết xuất đồ họa bằng GDI+ 32-bit ARGB với phông chữ hệ thống Segoe UI sắc nét, hỗ trợ tự động co giãn theo DPI trên từng màn hình.

  • Lịch sử thông minh:

  • Hiển thị thời gian chạy lệnh gần nhất ngay bên cạnh biểu tượng đồng hồ ở mỗi dòng.

  • Hỗ trợ bấm chọn nhanh, nhấp đúp để chạy ngay, hoặc dùng phím Lên / Xuống (↑ / ↓).

  • Thanh nhập liệu & Nút chức năng:

  • Ô nhập lệnh không viền, tự cuộn ngang khi đường dẫn dài.

  • Nút Duyệt (Duyệt 📁): Mở hộp thoại chọn tệp hệ thống (*.exe, *.bat, *.cmd, *.msc, *.cpl) và đưa đường dẫn lên thanh nhập.

  • Nút Chạy (Chạy ↵) & Thoát (Thoát ✕): Nổi bật, trực quan với hiệu ứng chuyển màu khi rê chuột.

  • Cải tiến trải nghiệm (Quality-of-Life):

  • Nhấn Win + R để đóng nhanh: Nhấn lại Win + R khi hộp thoại đang mở sẽ lập tức đóng hoặc khôi phục cửa sổ.

  • Tương thích hoàn hảo bộ gõ Tiếng Việt (IME): Hoạt động mượt mà với Unikey, EVKey và bộ gõ Windows, không bị lỗi khung trắng đè chữ.

entry.title: Windows 8/8.1 Charms Bar Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 8/8.1 Charms Bar Recreation

This mod recreates the classic Windows 8/8.1 Charms Bar on Windows 10 and 11.

Screenshots

Windows 8/8.1-styled Charms Bar

Windows 8 beta-styled Charms Bar

About the mod

It recreates the five charms (Search, Share, Start, Devices, Settings) with Win+C and edge activation, keyboard and touch input, multi-monitor placement, and a clock/status flyout. Suggestions are welcome. Tested on Windows 10 21H2, Windows 11 24H2 and Windows 11 25H2. Note: This is a best effort modification. Layout, colors, icons and animations are heavily inspired by Windows 8/8.1. Share, Devices and the Second screen panel are recreations on Windows 10/11, not the original code.

Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action | | --- | --- | | Win+C | Opens the Charms Bar | | Right-edge mouse gesture | Opens the Charms Bar | | Esc | Closes the rail or an open pane | | Click outside | Closes the rail or an open pane |

While a charm pane is open:

| Shortcut | Action | | --- | --- | | Win+C | Closes the current pane first | | Esc | Closes the current pane | | Click outside | Closes the current pane |

Settings

  • Charms Bar enabled: turns the Charms Bar on or off. Share is always included.
  • In-mod language: English, Italian, German, French, Spanish, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese (Simplified) or Korean. The choice applies to the rail, the charm panes and the Project panel alike.
  • Activation mode: full right edge, top-right corner, Win+C, or combinations.
  • Hide after choosing a charm: closes the Charms Bar after a charm is activated. Turn off to leave it open.
  • Close on outside click or focus change: light-dismiss behavior.
  • Animate show and hide: enables pane motion. Windows' own Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects > Animation effects switch is always honoured: when it is off, the rail and the panes appear and disappear instantly even if this setting is on.
  • Start logo style: Windows 8/8.1 logo (system accent) or the Windows 8 Build 8102 beta logo.
  • Charms Bar icons: Windows 8/8.1 icons, or the Windows 8 Build 8102 beta set for Search, Share, Devices and Settings. The Start logo is set separately.
  • Enable rail transparency: optional subtle rail transparency.
  • Show clock and system status flyout: shows or hides the clock and status flyout.
  • Settings pane color: system accent or dark background for the Settings, Devices and Share panes.
  • Settings charm: recreated Windows 8-style pane or native Win+I.
  • Search charm target: automatic or Windows search. Automatic opens the companion Windows 8/8.1 Search Charm Recreation panel when that mod is installed, otherwise it sends the Windows shortcut.
  • Search hand-off shortcut: automatic, Win+S, or Win+Q. Used only when the target is Windows search.
  • Share fallback behavior: automatic, Windows Share UI, Win+H, or mail/clipboard.
  • Display Switch panel title, color and custom color: see the project flyout settings at the end of the settings page.

Performance

Live system data (volume, brightness, network, battery) is read only while a pane or flyout is open. Rendering falls back to native GDI if GDI+ startup fails.

Requirements

  • Windows 10 version 1809 or later (64-bit), with DWM enabled (default on Windows)

Notes

  • The Charms Bar appears on the main monitor, where all five charms are displayed.

Credits

  • Icepenguins101 - Technical Inspiration
  • AdministratoX - Testing on Windows 11 25H2 and providing feedback
  • Kiyaku - Providing feedback
  • CharmsBarReloaded project - Wi-Fi PNGs and battery silhouettes (GPL-3.0, license-compatible)

entry.title: Where I Left It 1.2
entry.content:
Where I Left It

Remembers where you left each app's window -- its position, its size, and which monitor it was on -- and puts it back when the app opens again. It also keeps windows that are already open reachable when your display setup changes: a monitor going away, a different resolution, docking or undocking, or a rotation.

Getting started

The mod does nothing until you tell it which apps to manage. Open the mod's settings, add an executable name (for example notepad.exe) or a full path to Apps to manage, and save. Only windows belonging to the executables in that list are remembered or moved.

How it behaves

  • Geometry is captured when you move or resize a window, and when a window closes. Move a window where you want it, close it, and it opens there next time -- in the same session or after a reboot.
  • Maximized and minimized windows are handled as you would expect: a window that was maximized comes back maximized, and one that was minimized comes back where it was, at its normal size, or maximized if it was maximized before it was minimized.
  • Saving is per monitor arrangement. A window is restored to the same monitor it was on, and after docking or undocking it is mapped to the closest equivalent monitor instead of being left off-screen.
  • Windows that are already open are moved too. When the display arrangement changes -- a different resolution, docking, a monitor waking up or going away -- open tracked windows are mapped from the monitor they were on to the closest equivalent monitor that still exists, keeping the same fraction of that monitor. Nothing is left stranded on a monitor that is no longer there.
  • Moving or resizing a window always wins over anything the mod was doing. If an application insists on its own placement, the mod tries once more and then stops fighting it.
  • Each app's saved geometry can remember its position and its size separately, per app, in the settings. With Restore size off, a window is placed but not resized, so an app that sizes itself to its content keeps that size; with Restore position off, it is sized where it opened. Both are still recorded while off, so switching a box back on brings back the last position or size that window had rather than a value frozen at the moment it was switched off.

Out of scope in v1

  • Moving windows between virtual desktops
  • Z-order (stacking order) restore
  • Re-scaling what is inside a window when the scale percentage changes. The frame is moved and sized; how an app redraws its contents is up to the app.
  • A periodic check for monitor changes. The mod reacts to Windows' display-change notification and is silent the rest of the time.
  • UWP / Store apps that restore their own window placement

Known limitations

  • Elevated windows are not moved. Windows cannot be repositioned across integrity levels: the move is refused with access denied, the mod detects the refusal, leaves that window alone for the rest of the session, and records why. The window is still tracked, so it is not ignored -- the mod tries. While a refusal stands, that window's position is not saved either: your chosen position for it is not overwritten by wherever it happened to be sitting.
  • Titles are part of how a window is matched. A window whose title changed between sessions falls back to matching by executable, class and ordinal, and is only restored when that match is unambiguous. Windows with identical titles may be restored to each other's positions.
  • A save at close can lose its turn. The rectangle is read from the window as the window is closing, and Windows sometimes has the window out of the way first. When that happens nothing is recorded for that close, the diagnostics journal says so with a reason, and the window keeps whatever position it was last remembered at. Moving the window once by hand records it there and then, and that save is not a last-moment read, so this is about windows that are moved by something other than you and closed immediately after.
  • A window that was minimized when it closed comes back where it was, at its normal size, or maximized if it was maximized before it was minimized. It does not come back minimized.
  • Stored resolution is not rescaled when DPI changes. Nothing multiplies a stored rectangle by a DPI ratio. After a display change a window is mapped by the rules above, which already express it as a fraction of its monitor -- so a change of scale percentage on its own leaves windows where they are, because no monitor has moved.
  • A window is measured against the screen, not against the taskbar. The taskbar is taller in pixels at a larger scale, so a window restored after a change of scale percentage can sit partly behind it. Move the window once and the new position is what is remembered.
  • A maximized window is left where Windows puts it. While its monitor still exists, its maximized state and placement stay Windows' own business -- the mod does not move it, and it is not resized by a resolution change. If the monitor it was maximized on disappears, it is rescued onto a remaining monitor like any other window.
  • UWP and Store apps often restore their own placement and may ignore the mod.
  • If an application moves its window right after showing, the mod re-applies the stored geometry once. Applications that keep overriding it are left alone.

Diagnostics

Turn on Write a diagnostics journal in the settings and the mod appends a line to window-geometry-journal.txt for every save, restore and decision, with the exact rectangle and monitor involved. It is the fastest way to see why a particular window was or was not restored, and it is worth attaching to a bug report. It is off by default.

Both files live in a folder named after the signed-in user's SID, inside the mod's storage folder. That storage folder is shared by the whole machine and a tool mod runs one process per signed-in session, so the folder is created with a protected access control list that gives full access to that user, SYSTEM and administrators, and to nobody else: two users signed in at once neither overwrite each other's saved geometry nor can read each other's window titles. If the mod cannot read the user's SID it saves nothing at all -- sharing the data would be worse than forgetting it. The journal is a diagnostics aid rather than a history, so it is capped: once it passes a megabyte it starts over from empty.

entry.title: Taskbar Cat 1.0.4
entry.content:
Taskbar Cat

An orange pixel-art cat that lives on the Windows 11 taskbar.

The cat has moods. Energy, boredom and a need for attention drift over time and decide what it does next: strolls, the odd burst of zoomies, sitting, loafing, and naps when it gets tired (more of them at night). If you leave the PC for 5 minutes it curls up and sleeps until you come back.

Playing with it:

  • Hover over the cat: it purrs, with hearts.
  • Click: it meows (or wakes up).
  • Double-click: it rolls over for a belly rub.
  • Drag it: you pick it up by the scruff; let go and it drops back down.
  • Whizz the cursor along the taskbar near it: it may crouch, wiggle and pounce.
  • Right-click for a menu: pet, treat, nap, wake up, move over, "Stay here" (it keeps doing everything else but won't wander off; drag it to move it), let a butterfly in, or hide it for an hour.

It also notices Windows: it looks up (and sometimes jumps) when a new window opens, trots over to the taskbar buttons when one flashes, says hello when you unlock the PC, and hides during fullscreen apps and with an auto-hidden taskbar.

Between all that it grooms, scratches behind its ears, kneads before a nap, chases its own tail when bored, and stretches and yawns when it wakes up.

Toys: now and then a butterfly flutters along the taskbar and the cat stalks it (it catches one about a third of the time). Pick "Play with yarn" from the right-click menu to toss it a ball of yarn; click the ball to send it rolling, right-click it (or the cat) to put it away. Once in a while the cat leaves you a gift (a toy mouse): click it to collect it.

When music is playing it sits and bobs along to the beat (it listens to everything your PC plays, so videos and games count too). Around 8:00 and 19:00 it gets hungry and asks for a treat (right-click, "Give a treat"). It wears a witch hat in late October, a Santa hat in December, and a party hat on New Year's and on its own birthday. The tooltip shows how old it is ("day 2"); set its birthday in the settings.

It can meow, trill hello and purr out loud: turn on "Sounds" in the settings. The sounds are generated by the mod itself, and it stays quiet while Do Not Disturb is on or a fullscreen app is running.

Its mood, spot on the taskbar, age and your gift count are remembered across restarts.

The cat lives on the main taskbar only (not the taskbars of other monitors), and only on a horizontal taskbar. Everything above can be tuned or switched off in the settings.

Empty taskbar space stays click-through, and the cat hides with an auto-hidden taskbar or a fullscreen app.

entry.title: Folder thumbnails on taskbar buttons 1.0
entry.content:
Folder thumbnails on taskbar buttons

Every File Explorer window gets a taskbar icon showing the folder it has open, drawn the way Explorer draws that folder in its own large-icon view. A folder full of photos shows those photos on its taskbar button.

Without the mod, every File Explorer window has the same icon:

With the mod, each one shows the folder it has open:

Recommended: FolderThumbnailFix

The mod works best together with FolderThumbnailFix by LesFerch. Windows 11 draws the front of a folder over the folder's preview, which hides most of the pictures inside. FolderThumbnailFix removes that cover, so a taskbar button shows the pictures in full, as in the screenshot above.

No delay

The mod takes over the window procedure of each Explorer window. When Explorer changes a window's icon after a navigation or a tab switch, the mod substitutes the folder preview within that very message. The taskbar therefore gets a single icon update, at the same moment it would have received Explorer's own icon, and the generic folder icon never appears in between. A newly opened window gets its preview before it is shown for the first time.

Previews come from an in-memory cache, from the mod's own disk cache or from the Windows thumbnail cache. The disk cache is kept in the mod's Windhawk storage, in a folder which only your account can open, and is removed together with the mod. When a preview is in none of them, the button keeps Explorer's own folder icon and the preview is rendered in the background, usually within a fraction of a second, and then saved for next time.

No polling

The mod sleeps while nothing happens. It reacts to events: a window being shown, a navigation, a tab switch, a change among the files of an open folder, and a window being closed. A folder is re-rendered when its files change, and once in the background when it is opened again later, so that changes made while it was closed show up too. That refresh is usually served from the Windows thumbnail cache.

Requirements

  • Disable grouping on the taskbar with its "Use window icons" option. The mod puts the preview on each Explorer window, and that mod gives each window its own taskbar button and makes the button show the window's icon instead of the Explorer icon. To use window icons for File Explorer only, leave "Use window icons" off and add explorer.exe to "Use window icons exceptions".
  • Thumbnails enabled. In File Explorer, under Options -> View, the checkbox "Always show icons, never thumbnails" must be unchecked.

The mod has no settings. The preview resolution follows the screen's DPI, previews are kept on disk so that they are instant after a reboot, and the old ones are discarded once there are too many of them.

entry.title: Explorer Backspace Navigation 0.1.1
entry.content:
Explorer Backspace Navigation

Explorer normally uses Backspace to revisit the previous location. If that folder has been deleted or moved, it can show a "Location is not available" error instead of taking you to the parent folder.

The screenshot shows the standard Explorer error this mod's missing-folder fallback is designed to avoid.

Choose how unmodified Backspace navigates in File Explorer:

  • Always go to the parent folder (enabled by default): Backspace behaves like Alt+Up, regardless of navigation history. For example, from C:\test\foo it opens C:\test, even after visiting C:\test\foo\bar.
  • Switch disabled: Keep Explorer's normal history navigation. Before opening the previous location, check whether its filesystem folder still exists. If it was deleted, renamed, or moved, open the parent of the current folder instead. Other history entries are not searched or removed.

If several ancestors have been deleted, the mod chooses the nearest existing ancestor. At the Shell Desktop root there is no parent, so Backspace does nothing in the first mode.

Renaming, typing in the address/search bars, and dialogs keep their normal Backspace behavior. Shortcuts using Ctrl, Alt, Shift, or the Windows key, as well as the Back/Forward buttons, are unaffected. Settings apply immediately.

Scope and compatibility

Intended for 64-bit Windows 10 and Windows 11 Explorer, including tabbed windows. The browser is obtained through IShellWindows and matched to the focused tab or folder view. If it cannot be matched, native processing is kept. The mod does not maintain a separate history.

Initial user testing of version 0.1.1 reported working behavior after enabling the mod. Broader Windows-build and scenario coverage remains to be validated. The mod requires ExplorerFrame's CShellBrowser::_MayTranslateAccelerator symbol. If it is unavailable, initialization fails with a log message. Internal C++ object addresses are never used as COM interface pointers.

History checks cover absolute filesystem paths and file URLs, including Unicode and UNC paths. Virtual locations such as Home, This PC, searches, and archive views keep normal history navigation. If history cannot be read, the URL is not understood, or the existence check is inconclusive (for example, access denied), Explorer keeps its normal behavior. Such failures are not treated as proof that the folder was deleted.

Checks use normal filesystem I/O, so an unresponsive network location can delay the key press. A folder can also disappear between the check and Explorer opening it; this mod does not suppress unrelated error dialogs.

Enable this mod's debug logging in Windhawk to diagnose missing symbols, history-service failures, and navigation results. No files, history entries, or Explorer registry preferences are changed by the mod.

entry.title: Desktop Disk Icon 1.0.0
entry.content:
Desktop Disk Icon / 桌面显示U盘图标

中文描述在下方，请继续向下滚动查看。 English first; the Chinese section is at the bottom.

Renders external storage devices as native Windows desktop icons, in a manner comparable to how mounted volumes appear on the macOS desktop.

Features

  • Covers USB flash drives, external hard disks and SSDs, optical media (CD/DVD/Blu-ray and mounted ISO images), floppy disks and memory cards.
  • Only volumes are shown, matching macOS: phones (MTP/PTP, iPhone) are not mounted as volumes and therefore never appear on the desktop.
  • Icons are taken from the volume itself. The shell derives them from the volume label, autorun.inf or the device description; the mod never substitutes its own icons.
  • Icon names combine the volume label with the drive letter. When the label is empty, the device type name reported by the shell is used, for example U 盘 (F) or CD-ROM (H).

How it works

By default the mod registers a shell namespace item for each drive. Such an item belongs to the same category of desktop objects as "This PC" and "Recycle Bin": no .lnk file is created on the desktop and no shortcut arrow is drawn. The item is registered through the shell's built-in delegated folder (InProcServer32 is shell32.dll, Instance\InitPropertyBag\TargetFolderPath is the volume), so the shell uses its own folder object: no mod code is loaded by the shell or by any other process, and the item behaves exactly like a built-in folder.

The mod runs inside explorer.exe, listens for the shell's drive and media change notifications, and additionally polls at a configurable interval. Every synchronization pass brings the desktop icons in line with the devices that are currently attached.

Cleanup behaviour

  • Nothing is written to the system registry. The item definitions live in a private hive (RegLoadAppKey) inside the mod's storage, and four registry read hooks redirect Explorer's reads of Desktop\NameSpace and Software\Classes\CLSID to that hive. The items therefore exist only inside Explorer and vanish as soon as the mod is unloaded.
  • The bookkeeping values the shell writes under Shell Extensions\Cached are removed on unload.
  • Unplugging a device deletes the corresponding item; disabling or uninstalling the mod deletes every item created by it.
  • The mod only acts in the Explorer process that owns the desktop window; other explorer.exe instances (folder windows in a separate process, explorer.exe /select, and similar short-lived processes) are skipped, so the hooks never run there and those windows do not show the items.
  • Updating the mod takes effect immediately; no Explorer restart is required, because the item is served by the shell itself.

Known limitations

  • External hard disks are recognised by bus type (USB, IEEE 1394, SD/MMC, virtual). Disks attached through Thunderbolt or eSATA that report an internal bus may not be recognised; internal disks are never shown.
  • Portable devices (MTP/PTP, and phones in general) are not shown, because they are not volumes.
  • Removing a device deletes its icon immediately; there is no eject command. Use the system tray safe-removal function before unplugging.
  • If plugging or unplugging a disk does not update the desktop, set the polling interval to about 10 seconds in the settings.

Links

  • GitHub: https://github.com/AomiRaku/desktop-disk-icon

中文部分

功能

  • 覆盖 USB 闪存盘、外接硬盘与固态硬盘、光盘（CD/DVD/蓝光及已挂载的 ISO 映像）、软盘、 存储卡。
  • 只显示「卷」，与 macOS 一致：手机（MTP/PTP、iPhone）不会被挂载成卷，因此不会出现在桌面。
  • 图标取自磁盘本身，由系统依据卷标、autorun.inf 或设备描述提供，模组不做替换。
  • 图标名称由卷标与盘符组合而成；卷标为空时采用系统提供的设备类型名称， 例如 U 盘 (F)、CD-ROM (H)。

实现方式

默认情况下，模组为每个驱动器注册一个 shell 命名空间项，与“此电脑”“回收站”属于同一类桌面 对象：桌面不产生 .lnk 文件，也不显示快捷方式箭头。该项通过 shell 自带的委托文件夹注册 （InProcServer32 为 shell32.dll，Instance\InitPropertyBag\TargetFolderPath 为该卷根 目录），因此使用的是系统自己的文件夹对象：shell 与其他进程都不会加载模组代码，行为与系统 内置文件夹完全一致。

模组运行于 explorer.exe，监听 shell 的驱动器与介质变更通知，并以定时轮询作为补充； 每次同步均使桌面图标与当前设备状态保持一致。

清理行为

  • 不写系统注册表。 项的定义放在模组存储目录下的私有 hive 中（RegLoadAppKey），并用 4 个 注册表读取 hook 把资源管理器对 Desktop\NameSpace 与 Software\Classes\CLSID 的读取重定向 到该 hive。因此这些项只存在于资源管理器内部，模组卸载后立即消失。
  • 资源管理器写进 Shell Extensions\Cached 的书签值会在卸载时清除。
  • 拔出设备时删除对应项；禁用或卸载模组时删除全部由本模组创建的项目。
  • 模组只在拥有桌面窗口的资源管理器进程中工作；其他 explorer.exe 实例（在单独进程中打开 文件夹窗口、explorer.exe /select, 等短命进程）会被跳过：hook 不会装在那里，那些窗口也 不会显示这些项。
  • 更新模组即时生效，无需重启资源管理器（项本身由系统实现）。

已知限制

  • 外接硬盘依据设备总线类型识别（USB、IEEE 1394、SD/MMC、虚拟）；雷雳或 eSATA 接口且被报告为 内置总线的硬盘可能无法识别，内置磁盘始终不会显示。
  • 便携设备（MTP/PTP 及手机）不显示，因为它们不是卷。
  • 拔出设备时直接移除图标，不提供弹出操作；请沿用系统托盘中的安全删除功能。
  • 若插拔磁盘后桌面未更新，可在设置中将轮询间隔设为 10 秒左右。

相关链接

  • GitHub：https://github.com/AomiRaku/desktop-disk-icon
